68	
69	Ask what the reader is doing when they open the page.
70	
71	| The reader is | Job | It holds | It leaves out |
72	|---|---|---|---|
73	| learning by doing | Tutorial | one path that works, a visible result at every step | options, alternatives, explanation beyond a clause |
74	| working toward a goal | How-to guide | the steps to that goal, for a competent reader | teaching, background, the full list of options |

87	mention, find its actor now. Run a command to confirm it only when the run changes
88	nothing (a read, `--help`, a dry run). Keep a list of what you could not confirm.

94	where it falls, as a `TODO` that says what is missing. Never paper over a hole, and list
95	every one in the reply.

100	and ask "who or what does this?" The sentence has to answer.

107	
108	- **A passive without its agent.** "The cache is invalidated on deploy" becomes "The
109	  deploy job invalidates the cache".
110	- **A noun that swallowed the verb.** "After validation of the token" becomes "After the

115	  has several parts. Name the part.

122

124	  audit log does not record by whom."

129	follows one thing through the system and that thing should stay at the front of the
130	sentence, give it an active verb: "The request then goes to the gateway, which signs it".

134	Portuguese, or when you review a text you did not write.

149	- After a revision, the reply says what changed in three lines at most and retells
150	  nothing the document says. The user has the file.

153	
154	### The document
155	
156	- Lead with the point. The first paragraph says what the thing is and what the reader
157	  gets from the page, in words they would search for. Many readers stop there.
158	- State what the document covers, and what it leaves out that a reader would expect to
159	  find. Put prerequisites before the first step.
160	- A heading says what its section holds. A heading for a task starts with a verb.
161	- Cut what the reader's task does not need. Link to a detail instead of repeating it.
162	
163	### The paragraph
164	
165	- The first sentence states the point of the paragraph. One topic per paragraph.
166	- Start a sentence with what the reader already has, and end it with what is new. The
167	  end of the sentence is where the reader puts the emphasis.
168	- Use a numbered list for a sequence, bullets for parallel items, a table for items
169	  compared on the same attributes, and prose for reasoning, because a list drops the
170	  connectives. Introduce a list with a full sentence and keep its items parallel.
171

173	
174	- Actor, verb, object, in that order, with the subject next to its verb.
175	- Let the verb carry the action: "validates", not "performs the validation of".
176	- One idea per sentence. Put the condition before the instruction: "To roll back, run…",
177	  "If the check fails, restart the worker".
178	- Present tense. Address the reader as "you", in the form of address the house uses.
179	- Prefer the positive form, and never stack negatives: "the job retries once the lock
180	  is free", not "the job does not retry unless the lock is not held".
181	- Write the number with its unit, and the exact name. "Slow" and "some errors" cannot be
182	  acted on, and "p95 above 800 ms" and "`ERR_QUOTA`" can.
183

185

187	  second thing.
188	- Define a term where it first appears. Spell an acronym out once, and only when the
189	  document uses it several times.
190	- "It", "this", and "they" point at one noun the reader has just read. Otherwise repeat
191	  the noun.
192	- Identifiers, commands, paths, and values go in code font, spelled as in the source.
193	- Leave "simply", "just", "easy", and "obviously" out of instructions. They tell the
194	  reader who is stuck that the fault is theirs.

199	  before what: "In `config/app.yaml`, set…".

201	- After a step with a result the reader can check, show that result.
202	- A command block holds only what the reader types, with no prompt character. Mark a
203	  placeholder as `<name>` and say what replaces it.
204	- A sample runs as written, is as small as the point allows, and says how to run it and
205	  what it prints.

210	every fact (contract 4), and change what the rules above call for. A passive whose actor
211	the repository does not give stays as it is and becomes a question in the reply. Do not
212	delete the sentence and do not guess.
213	
214	**"Review".** Report before editing, in two groups: questions for the author (an actor
215	or a fact that only they know, a reader the document never settles) and proposed edits,
216	each with its reason. Quote the sentence. Apply what the user chooses.

222	tool-parsed text belong to the calling skill and stay as they are. An actor nobody
223	established goes where that skill puts its open questions. Add no report of your own.
224

226

228	- **A revision.** Edit in place, report the path, and say in at most three lines what
229	  changed.
230	- **A short text** (a pull request description, a commit message). Reply with the text
231	  ready to paste. Do not post or commit it unless the user asked.
232	
233	After the result, list only what applies: the reader you assumed, the questions left
234	open, and the commands you did not run. Do not summarize the document.
235	
236	## Reference files
237	
238	| File | Read it when |
239	|---|---|
240	| `references/documents.md` | Before writing or reviewing a specific kind of document: what each one must hold, its order, and its usual failure. |
241	| `references/actors.md` | A sentence resists the actor pass, the document is in Portuguese, or you review a text you did not write. |
242

244	
245	The layered structure follows the `technical-writing` skill of
246	[pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) by Lauren Tan, licensed MIT.
247	The rule that every verb has an actor follows Tanya Reilly's *The Staff Engineer's Path*.

251	Judith Swan's "The Science of Scientific Writing". The "by zombies" test is Rebecca
252	Johnson's. See `NOTICE.md`.

8	
9	- The test

13	- Notes for Portuguese
14	- "We", "you", and the software

17	
18	Take one verb at a time, including the verbs buried in nouns ("validation",
19	"configuração"). Ask "who or what does this?" Then check two things: the sentence
20	answers, and the answer is the grammatical subject. A sentence can pass the first and
21	fail the second ("validation is performed by the gateway"), and then the fix is only a
22	reordering.
23	
24	For the grammatical passive there is a faster detector, Rebecca Johnson's: insert "by
25	zombies" after the verb, or at the end of the clause when an object is in the way. If
26	the sentence still reads as a sentence, the verb is passive.
27	
28	| Sentence | With zombies | Verdict |
29	|---|---|---|
30	| The token is validated before the request is forwarded. | The token is validated [by zombies] before the request is forwarded [by zombies]. | Two passives, two actors to look up. |
31	| The gateway validates the token. | The gateway validates [by zombies] the token. | Not a sentence. Active. |
32	| O token é validado antes do envio. | O token é validado [por zumbis] antes do envio. | Passive. "Envio" hides a second verb that the zombies do not catch. |
33	
34	The zombies have two limits. They find the form and not the other five hiding places: a
35	noun that swallowed the verb, an empty subject, a catch-all actor, a described
36	instruction, and the Portuguese forms with "se" all pass the test and still hide the
37	actor. And they also fit a state ("The service is written in Go [by zombies]"), which is
38	one of the passives that stay. Use the test to find candidates, then decide each one
39	with the question.
40	
41	The question is about information, not about grammar. A passive that names its actor has
42	lost nothing but directness. A passive without one has dropped a fact. Spend the effort
43	on the second kind.
44	
45	## Where the actor hides
46	
47	### A passive without its agent
48	
49	| Before | After |
50	|---|---|
51	| The data is encrypted before it is stored. | The `ledger` service encrypts the data before it writes the data to PostgreSQL. |
52	| Failed jobs are retried three times. | The worker retries a failed job three times. |
53	| Os dados são criptografados antes de serem gravados. | O serviço `ledger` criptografa os dados antes de gravá-los no PostgreSQL. |
54	| Os jobs com falha são reprocessados três vezes. | O worker reprocessa três vezes cada job que falha. |
55	
56	A sentence often hides two actors. "The token is validated and the request is forwarded"
57	may be one component or two. Look both up.
58	
59	### A noun that swallowed the verb
60	
61	| Before | After |
62	|---|---|
63	| After validation of the token, forwarding of the request occurs. | After the gateway validates the token, it forwards the request to the `orders` service. |
64	| Rotation of the keys happens monthly. | A scheduled job, `rotate-keys`, rotates the keys on the first day of each month. |
65	| Após a validação do token, ocorre o encaminhamento da requisição. | Depois de validar o token, o gateway encaminha a requisição ao serviço `orders`. |
66

68	"-mento", "-agem". Verbs such as "occur", "happen", "take place", "ocorrer", and
69	"realizar" next to one of them confirm the pattern.
70	
71	### A subject that means nothing
72	
73	| Before | After |
74	|---|---|
75	| It is recommended to enable the cache. | The platform team recommends enabling the cache. *Or, as an instruction:* Enable the cache. |
76	| There is a timeout of 30 seconds. | The client gives up after 30 seconds. |
77	| É necessário reiniciar o serviço após a mudança. | Reinicie o serviço depois de mudar o arquivo. |
78	| Existe uma verificação de permissão. | O middleware `authz` verifica a permissão. |
79	
80	"It is recommended" hides who recommends. When nobody in particular does, the sentence
81	is an instruction, so write it as one.
82	
83	### A catch-all actor
84	
85	| Before | After |
86	|---|---|
87	| The system sends a notification. | The `notifier` worker sends an email to the account owner. |
88	| The application handles the error. | The `orders` handler catches the error and returns `503`. |
89	| O sistema envia uma notificação. | O worker `notifier` envia um e-mail ao titular da conta. |
90	
91	"The system" is an actor only when the system has one part, or when the document is for
92	a reader who sees it from outside and has no use for the parts. "Handles", "manages",
93	"processes", "trata", and "gerencia" usually travel with the catch-all actor. Replace them with
94	what the component does.
95	
96	### An instruction written as a description
97	
98	| Before | After |
99	|---|---|
100	| The `DATABASE_URL` variable must be set. | Set `DATABASE_URL`. |
101	| The migration should be run before the deploy. | Run the migration before you deploy. |
102	| A variável `DATABASE_URL` deve ser definida. | Defina `DATABASE_URL`. |
103	
104	When the reader is not the one who acts, say who is: "The CI pipeline runs the migration
105	before each deploy. You do not run it by hand."
106	
107	## When the source does not name the actor
108	
109	Look in this order: the code path, the configuration and the deployment files, the
110	existing docs, the conversation. Then:
111	
112	- **Writing a new document.** If the reader's task depends on the actor, ask the user
113	  before writing. If it does not, leave the sentence out and list the question in the
114	  reply.
115	- **Revising someone's text.** Keep the sentence as the author wrote it and put the
116	  question in the reply: "'Backups are rotated weekly': nothing in the repository says
117	  what rotates them. Who or what does?"
118	- **Called by another skill.** The question goes where that skill puts its open
119	  questions.
120	
121	Never settle it with "the system", and never promote a likely candidate. A reader who
122	knows the real actor stops trusting the rest of the document.
123	
124	## The passives that stay
125	
126	**The actor is unknown.** Common in a postmortem and in a bug report. Say that it is
127	unknown, so that the reader does not take the gap for an omission: "The flag was turned
128	off at 09:40. The audit trail was not enabled, so we do not know by whom."
129	
130	**The verb describes a state.** "The library is licensed under MIT." "The table is
131	partitioned by month." "O serviço é escrito em Go." Nobody asks "by whom?", and a rewrite
132	would invent an actor to satisfy a rule. The check is the question itself. If a reader
133	could need the answer ("the certificate is renewed every 60 days"), the verb describes
134	an action.
135	
136	A passive that names its actor with "by" does not stay. It hides nothing, and it is
137	tempting in a paragraph that follows one thing through a pipeline, because a sentence
138	reads best when it begins with what the reader already holds. Keep that thing at the
139	front and give it an active verb instead:
140	
141	| Before | After |
142	|---|---|
143	| The message is then enriched by the `geo` consumer, which adds the region, and stored by the `archive` consumer. | The message then goes to the `geo` consumer, which adds the region, and to the `archive` consumer, which stores it. |
144	| A requisição é então assinada pelo gateway. | A requisição segue para o gateway, que a assina. |
145	
146	Verbs that let the object lead are "goes to", "reaches", "passes through", "arrives
147	at", and in Portuguese "segue para", "chega a", "passa por".
148	
149	## Notes for Portuguese
150	
151	- **Voz passiva analítica**: "é enviado", "foi configurado", "será validado". Same
152	  rewrite as in English.
153	- **Voz passiva sintética e sujeito indeterminado**: "envia-se", "configura-se o
154	  serviço", "precisa-se de", "deve-se executar". Shorter than the analytic passive, and
155	  the actor is just as absent. In an instruction, use the imperative: "Execute".
156	- **Infinitivo impessoal**: "É preciso reiniciar", "Basta rodar". Write the instruction
157	  ("Reinicie") or the actor ("O deploy reinicia").
158	- **Steps in the infinitive** ("Executar o script", "Abrir o painel") are a house style
159	  in some teams. Follow the docs already in the repository. With no precedent, use the
160	  imperative, in the form of address those docs or the conversation use ("Execute",
161	  "Rode").
162	- Keep the identifiers and the technical terms the team uses in English as they are. Do
163	  not translate a component name.
164	
165	## "We", "you", and the software

168	- "We" is the team that owns the document, and only that. Do not use it for the software

171	- The software is named: the component, the command, the function. In a reference page

The nouns to watch end in "-tion", "-ment", "-ance", "-al", and in Portuguese in "-ção",
"-mento", "-agem". Verbs such as "occur", "happen", "take place", "ocorrer", and
"realizar" next to one of them confirm the pattern.

### A subject that means nothing

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| It is recommended to enable the cache. | The platform team recommends enabling the cache. *Or, as an instruction:* Enable the cache. |
| There is a timeout of 30 seconds. | The client gives up after 30 seconds. |
| É necessário reiniciar o serviço após a mudança. | Reinicie o serviço depois de mudar o arquivo. |
| Existe uma verificação de permissão. | O middleware `authz` verifica a permissão. |

"It is recommended" hides who recommends. When nobody in particular does, the sentence
is an instruction, so write it as one.

### A catch-all actor

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| The system sends a notification. | The `notifier` worker sends an email to the account owner. |
| The application handles the error. | The `orders` handler catches the error and returns `503`. |
| O sistema envia uma notificação. | O worker `notifier` envia um e-mail ao titular da conta. |

"The system" is an actor only when the system has one part, or when the document is for
a reader who sees it from outside and has no use for the parts. "Handles", "manages",
"processes", "trata", and "gerencia" usually travel with the catch-all actor. Replace them with
what the component does.

### An instruction written as a description

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| The `DATABASE_URL` variable must be set. | Set `DATABASE_URL`. |
| The migration should be run before the deploy. | Run the migration before you deploy. |
| A variável `DATABASE_URL` deve ser definida. | Defina `DATABASE_URL`. |

When the reader is not the one who acts, say who is: "The CI pipeline runs the migration
before each deploy. You do not run it by hand."

## When the source does not name the actor

Look in this order: the code path, the configuration and the deployment files, the
existing docs, the conversation. Then:

- **Writing a new document.** If the reader's task depends on the actor, ask the user
  before writing. If it does not, leave the sentence out and list the question in the
  reply.
- **Revising someone's text.** Keep the sentence as the author wrote it and put the
  question in the reply: "'Backups are rotated weekly': nothing in the repository says
  what rotates them. Who or what does?"
- **Called by another skill.** The question goes where that skill puts its open
  questions.

Never settle it with "the system", and never promote a likely candidate. A reader who
knows the real actor stops trusting the rest of the document.

## The passives that stay

**The actor is unknown.** Common in a postmortem and in a bug report. Say that it is
unknown, so that the reader does not take the gap for an omission: "The flag was turned
off at 09:40. The audit trail was not enabled, so we do not know by whom."

**The verb describes a state.** "The library is licensed under MIT." "The table is
partitioned by month." "O serviço é escrito em Go." Nobody asks "by whom?", and a rewrite
would invent an actor to satisfy a rule. The check is the question itself. If a reader
could need the answer ("the certificate is renewed every 60 days"), the verb describes
an action.

A passive that names its actor with "by" does not stay. It hides nothing, and it is
tempting in a paragraph that follows one thing through a pipeline, because a sentence
reads best when it begins with what the reader already holds. Keep that thing at the
front and give it an active verb instead:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| The message is then enriched by the `geo` consumer, which adds the region, and stored by the `archive` consumer. | The message then goes to the `geo` consumer, which adds the region, and to the `archive` consumer, which stores it. |
| A requisição é então assinada pelo gateway. | A requisição segue para o gateway, que a assina. |

Verbs that let the object lead are "goes to", "reaches", "passes through", "arrives
at", and in Portuguese "segue para", "chega a", "passa por".

## Notes for Portuguese

- **Voz passiva analítica**: "é enviado", "foi configurado", "será validado". Same
  rewrite as in English.
- **Voz passiva sintética e sujeito indeterminado**: "envia-se", "configura-se o
  serviço", "precisa-se de", "deve-se executar". Shorter than the analytic passive, and
  the actor is just as absent. In an instruction, use the imperative: "Execute".
- **Infinitivo impessoal**: "É preciso reiniciar", "Basta rodar". Write the instruction
  ("Reinicie") or the actor ("O deploy reinicia").
- **Steps in the infinitive** ("Executar o script", "Abrir o painel") are a house style
  in some teams. Follow the docs already in the repository. With no precedent, use the
  imperative, in the form of address those docs or the conversation use ("Execute",
  "Rode").
- Keep the identifiers and the technical terms the team uses in English as they are. Do
  not translate a component name.

## "We", "you", and the software

- "You" is the reader. In a procedure the imperative already says so.
- "We" is the team that owns the document, and only that. Do not use it for the software
  ("we then parse the file") or for the reader and the writer together, except in a
  tutorial, where "we" walking through the steps is a convention.
- The software is named: the component, the command, the function. In a reference page
  the thing described is the actor of its own entry: "`retry()` returns the last error".

# Export pipeline

This page describes what happens to an export request.

## Request

When an export is requested, the payload is validated. Requests above 100,000 rows are
rejected. If the payload is valid, a job is enqueued and a `202` is returned.

## Processing

The job is picked up and the CSV file is generated. The file is encrypted before it is
uploaded to the bucket. If something goes wrong, the job is retried up to three times,
after which it is moved to the dead-letter queue.

## Delivery

Once the upload is done, a download link is sent by email. The link is expired after
24 hours.

## Backups

Backups of the bucket are rotated weekly.
"""Move messages from exports.dead back to exports.

    uv run python scripts/requeue_dead.py --dry-run    count the messages, move nothing
    uv run python scripts/requeue_dead.py --limit 50   move at most 50 messages
"""
import argparse
import os

import pika


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=100)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.URLParameters(os.environ["QUEUE_URL"]))
    channel = connection.channel()
    moved = 0
    while moved < args.limit:
        method, properties, body = channel.basic_get("exports.dead")
        if method is None:
            break
        if args.dry_run:
            channel.basic_nack(method.delivery_tag, requeue=True)
        else:
            channel.basic_publish(exchange="", routing_key="exports", body=body)
            channel.basic_ack(method.delivery_tag)
        moved += 1
    print(f"{'would move' if args.dry_run else 'moved'} {moved} message(s)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
import os

import pika
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException

app = FastAPI()
MAX_ROWS = 100_000


def validate_payload(payload: dict) -> None:
    if "account_id" not in payload:
        raise HTTPException(422, "account_id is required")
    if payload.get("rows", 0) > MAX_ROWS:
        raise HTTPException(413, f"exports above {MAX_ROWS} rows are not supported")


@app.post("/exports", status_code=202)
def create_export(payload: dict) -> dict:
    validate_payload(payload)
    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.URLParameters(os.environ["QUEUE_URL"]))
    channel = connection.channel()
    channel.basic_publish(exchange="", routing_key="exports", body=json.dumps(payload))
    connection.close()
    return {"status": "queued"}
import os

import boto3

LINK_TTL_SECONDS = 24 * 60 * 60


def notify(account_id: str, key: str) -> None:
    url = boto3.client("s3").generate_presigned_url(
        "get_object",
        Params={"Bucket": os.environ["EXPORT_BUCKET"], "Key": key},
        ExpiresIn=LINK_TTL_SECONDS,
    )
    boto3.client("ses").send_email(
        Source=os.environ["MAIL_FROM"],
        Destination={"ToAddresses": [f"{account_id}@accounts.example.com"]},
        Message={
            "Subject": {"Data": "Your export is ready"},
            "Body": {"Text": {"Data": url}},
        },
    )
import json
import os

import boto3
import pika
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

from exporter.notifier import notify

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3


def build_csv(job: dict) -> bytes:
    rows = [f"{job['account_id']},{n}" for n in range(job.get("rows", 0))]
    return "\n".join(rows).encode()


def handle(channel, method, properties, body) -> None:
    job = json.loads(body)
    attempts = (properties.headers or {}).get("x-attempts", 0) + 1
    try:
        data = Fernet(os.environ["EXPORT_KEY"]).encrypt(build_csv(job))
        key = f"{job['account_id']}/{method.delivery_tag}.csv.enc"
        boto3.client("s3").put_object(Bucket=os.environ["EXPORT_BUCKET"], Key=key, Body=data)
        notify(job["account_id"], key)
    except Exception:
        target = "exports.dead" if attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS else "exports"
        channel.basic_publish(
            exchange="",
            routing_key=target,
            body=body,
            properties=pika.BasicProperties(headers={"x-attempts": attempts}),
        )
    channel.basic_ack(method.delivery_tag)


def main() -> None:
    connection = pika.BlockingConnection(pika.URLParameters(os.environ["QUEUE_URL"]))
    channel = connection.channel()
    channel.basic_consume(queue="exports", on_message_callback=handle)
    channel.start_consuming()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

# Runbook: `ExportsDeadLetterHigh`

Este runbook é para quem está de plantão quando o alerta `ExportsDeadLetterHigh` dispara. Ele diz como confirmar o problema, como reduzir o impacto e quando chamar ajuda. Ele não explica o pipeline inteiro: para isso, leia [`docs/pipeline.md`](pipeline.md).

## O alerta

- **Nome:** `ExportsDeadLetterHigh`, severidade `page` (definido em `deploy/alerts.yaml`).
- **Resumo no pager:** "More than 10 exports failed three times".
- **Condição:** `rabbitmq_queue_messages{queue="exports.dead"} > 10`, durante 5 minutos seguidos.

A fila `exports.dead` guarda os pedidos de exportação que o worker (`exporter/worker.py`) tentou processar três vezes sem sucesso. O alerta dispara quando passam de 10 pedidos nessa fila.

## Impacto

Cada mensagem em `exports.dead` é um cliente que pediu uma exportação e não recebeu o e-mail com o link de download. O gateway já respondeu `202` a esse cliente, então ele espera o arquivo e não sabe que o pedido falhou. O alerta não indica que a API está fora: o gateway continua aceitando pedidos.

TODO: definir a urgência real (SLA da exportação, horário comercial ou 24x7). Nada no repositório diz isso.

## Antes de começar

- Você precisa da variável `QUEUE_URL` (a URL do RabbitMQ) no seu terminal e do `uv` instalado. O `Makefile` roda `uv sync` no alvo `setup`.
- Rode os comandos a partir da raiz do repositório.

TODO: dizer onde o plantão consegue o `QUEUE_URL` de produção e onde o repositório deve estar clonado (host, bastion, pod).

## 1. Confirme o alerta

1. Conte as mensagens em `exports.dead` sem mover nenhuma:

   ```bash
   uv run python scripts/requeue_dead.py --dry-run --limit 1000
   ```

   Saída esperada, com o alerta ativo:

   ```text
   would move 11 message(s)
   ```

   Um número acima de 10 confirma o alerta. O comando devolve cada mensagem à fila, então não altera nada. Sem `--limit`, ele conta no máximo 100 mensagens.

2. Se o número for 10 ou menos, o alerta já se resolveu ou o painel está atrasado. Espere 5 minutos e rode o comando de novo antes de encerrar o chamado.

TODO: link do painel do RabbitMQ/Prometheus onde o plantão vê `rabbitmq_queue_messages{queue="exports.dead"}` ao longo do tempo.

## 2. Descubra a causa antes de reenfileirar

Reenfileirar sem corrigir a causa só devolve as mensagens à `exports.dead`: o worker tenta cada uma mais três vezes e falha de novo.

O worker captura qualquer exceção e republica a mensagem **sem registrar o erro** (`except Exception` em `exporter/worker.py`). Por isso, o log do worker não mostra a causa, e a mensagem na fila também não a guarda. Em uma tentativa, o worker executa estes passos em ordem, e qualquer um deles pode ser o que falha:

1. Gera o CSV a partir do pedido (`build_csv`).
2. Criptografa o CSV com a chave da variável `EXPORT_KEY`.
3. Grava o arquivo no bucket definido em `EXPORT_BUCKET` (S3, `put_object`).
4. Envia o e-mail com o link, pelo SES, usando `MAIL_FROM` (`exporter/notifier.py`).

Use esta ordem para investigar:

1. Verifique se o worker está rodando e se consome a fila `exports`. Um worker parado deixa a fila `exports` crescer, mas não enche `exports.dead` sozinho.
2. Verifique as quatro dependências do worker: `EXPORT_KEY` definida e válida, acesso de escrita ao bucket `EXPORT_BUCKET`, e permissão do SES para enviar de `MAIL_FROM`. Uma falha comum a todas as mensagens (todas as mensagens falham da mesma forma) aponta para uma dessas configurações ou para uma queda do S3 ou do SES.
3. Se só alguns pedidos falham, o problema está no conteúdo desses pedidos.

TODO: onde o plantão lê os logs e as métricas do worker, e como inspecionar o corpo de uma mensagem em `exports.dead` (console do RabbitMQ ou outro). Nada no repositório descreve isso.

TODO: como o worker é executado em produção (serviço, container, cluster) e como reiniciá-lo. O repositório só traz `make run-worker` para uso local.

## 3. Reenfileire as mensagens

Faça isso só depois de corrigir a causa. Enquanto a causa existir, pare aqui e escale (seção 4).

> **Atenção: possível e-mail duplicado.** Se a falha ocorreu no envio do e-mail (passo 4 do worker), o arquivo já está no bucket. O worker grava um arquivo novo a cada tentativa e envia outro e-mail ao reprocessar, então o cliente pode receber mais de um e-mail.

1. Reenfileire um lote pequeno para testar:

   ```bash
   uv run python scripts/requeue_dead.py --limit 5
   ```

   Saída esperada:

   ```text
   moved 5 message(s)
   ```

2. Espere o worker processar o lote e confirme que `exports.dead` não voltou a crescer (repita o comando `--dry-run` da seção 1). Se as 5 mensagens voltaram à fila, a causa continua ativa: pare e escale.
3. Reenfileire o restante em lotes:

   ```bash
   uv run python scripts/requeue_dead.py --limit 50
   ```

   Repita até o comando imprimir `moved 0 message(s)`.

O script publica cada mensagem em `exports` sem o cabeçalho `x-attempts`, então o worker conta as tentativas do zero: cada mensagem ganha mais três tentativas.

## Como desfazer

O script não tem comando de desfazer. Uma mensagem reenfileirada que falha de novo volta sozinha a `exports.dead` depois de três tentativas. Não há outra forma de recolocar uma mensagem em `exports.dead`.

## 4. Escale

Escale quando:

- o `--dry-run` ainda mostra mensagens depois de você corrigir a causa e reenfileirar um lote de teste;
- você não consegue identificar a causa na seção 2;
- o número de mensagens em `exports.dead` continua crescendo.

TODO: nome do time dono do serviço `exporter`, política de escalonamento (quem acionar primeiro, quem em seguida) e canal de comunicação (Slack, telefone, ferramenta de plantão). O repositório não traz nenhum desses dados, e este runbook não os inventa.

## Depois do incidente

Reenfileirar resolve as mensagens atuais, mas não registra a causa. Anote a causa e a correção no canal do incidente. Como o worker não registra o erro, quem investigou é a única fonte dessa informação.
